result.title: Social Signal Bench: Evidence-Weighted Evaluation of Co-occurring Social Signals in Video and Audio
result.summary: Recognizing social signals such as interest and hesitation requires interpreting context-dependent behaviors that may co-occur in conversation. Existing affective computing benchmarks rarely evaluate such co-occurring signals, and conventional multi-label F1 overlooks semantic relationships and annotator disagreement. We introduce Social Signal Bench, a 47-hour densely annotated benchmark for the evaluation of social signal recognition and engagement, comprising two datasets: Social Signal Bench Video (25 hours), covering ten social signals in audiovisual recordings, and Social Signal Bench Audio (22 hours), covering six signals in audio-only recordings. Each dataset pairs a public training set of online conversational video, of which 10 hours are expert-annotated and the remainder pseudo-labeled, with a private expert-labeled test set spanning four conversational domains. We also propose Evidence-Weighted F1 (EW-F1), which weights reference labels by annotator evidence and assigns graded credit to semantically related predictions through optimal per-clip matching. Controlled perturbations demonstrate that EW-F1 distinguishes semantically related errors from unrelated ones, unlike conventional F1. Under a shared evaluation protocol, 7B open models post-trained on Social Signal Bench outperform general-purpose frontier models on video and match them on audio.

AI.brief_summary: 该文构建了 47 小时、密集标注的社交信号识别基准（视频 25 小时、音频 22 小时），覆盖共现的兴趣、迟疑等信号，并提出按标注证据加权、对语义相关预测给分级得分的 EW-F1 指标。
AI.relevance_reason: 其处理标注歧义与共现标签的分级评价思路，可能供核查 LVR 中多个 latent 假设或模糊证据的评分方式；但「证据」指标注者证据而非推理期视觉证据筛选，与内部状态生成无直接联系。
